## Triage 注记 · R+41 —— **无 `pm:*` 是正确的**,本卡由父卡定序

本卡曾被本席列入「有 `domain:*` 无 `pm:*` ⇒ 对车道队列查询不可见」的清单。**复核后撤回该判定。**

本卡是 **#12243 的子卡**,而 #12243 带 `pm:epic` · `tracking` · **`priority:p0`** ⇒ 它经**父卡**被触达与定序,⛔ 不是"沉默不可见"。

⇒ **本轮不加 `pm:*`**,理由是加了反而可能让它脱离 epic 的排序被单独取走。若 epic 的持有者认为它应当可独立认领,由**该 epic 的持有席**打标签,⛔ 不是 triage 越过 epic 去打。

⚠️ 一并记录一条对本席**对账口径的更正**:「有 domain 无 pm 状态」这个类别**必须排除 `pm:epic` 的子卡**。本席连续四轮在收班简报里把该类别称作"沉默不可见"而从未复核 —— 实测 5 张里 **3 张**并非如此(本卡与 #13274 是父卡定序;#12767 已于 2026-08-30T05:06Z 由 PR #13339 关闭)。该口径已更正,不再复述旧说法。

## Truncation repaired — the card is dispatchable again

The repair triage asked for on 2026-08-25 (`issuecomment-5414435717`) has been done: the body is rewritten with every angle-bracketed token in backticks, so it survives the sanitizer this time.

⚠️ **It is a re-measurement, not a recovery.** The original text is unrecoverable, so the new body is built from `origin/main` @ `479ace6` plus what #12237 and the epic record about this card's role. If the original carried anything the new body misses, @os-zhuang or the #12243 epic PM should add it — I have not tried to guess at intent beyond what is measurable.

**What the re-measurement changed versus the card's own title:**

- The title says *"one title serves SERP, h1, nav and llms.txt"* — four consumers. The measured count is **six**: the OG card image (`app/og/docs/[...slug]/route.tsx:18`) and the JSON-LD `BreadcrumbList` / `headline` (`page.tsx:95,123,124`) read the same string. Those two are the ones a title-lengthening PR reshapes silently.
- The premise itself holds exactly as stated: **405 pages, frontmatter keys in use are `title` (405) and `description` (405), and nothing else.** No page carries any nav-label field.

**Why this was worth doing now rather than at the epic's convenience:** this card is the enabling half of **#12237** (p1, `Blocked-by: #12311`), whose 176 remaining title rewrites cannot start until a short nav label exists — 4 of its 180 rows landed and the commit message names *"sidebar-free"* as the reason it stopped. A truncated body is not dispatchable, so the truncation alone was holding a p1 card under a p0 epic for seven days.

⛔ **No `pm:*` label added** — the 2026-08-30 triage note (`issuecomment-5467201509`) ruled that this card is sequenced through its parent #12243 and that a state label could pull it out of the epic's ordering. That ruling is untouched; queueing it remains the epic PM's call.

Standing authorization — the maintainer's direct-dispatch channel, invoked in this session verbatim: 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 派发处理」, against the explicitly named backlog filter `is:issue state:open label:pm:blocking`. This card carries `pm:blocking`, so it is inside the named set.

### Selection rationale — this is the only dispatchable card in the named set

All 23 open `pm:blocking` cards were read this round. **22 fail the candidate filter**: 5 in flight with another seat's assignee, 5 `pm:blocked` on an open upstream, 5 legally `pm:on-hold`, 3 `repo:cloud` and structurally unreachable, 2 epic parents, 1 `needs-user-decision`, 1 `tracking` coordination parent whose subtree is 5/5 complete. `pm:blocking` is a *priority ordering signal inside the queue*, ⛔ not a queue of its own — that is why the filter yields almost nothing dispatchable.

This card became dispatchable **this round**: its body was sanitizer-truncated on 2026-08-25 and repaired today, and "a truncated card is not dispatchable" was the only thing holding it. It gates **#12237** (p1, 176 title rewrites) under **p0 epic #12243**, so its unlock fan-out is the largest in the set.

## PM adjudication of the two open questions — both **A**, neither is a maintainer-floor item

`domain:devx` dispatch, session `session_014iv4atze36k7F9C8oAe7QL`, R1. Reviewer of record. ⚠️ **This is not the ACCEPT** — CI has been running 4 minutes and a verdict on a converging farm is worth nothing. Verdict follows at the check-in. Adjudicating now because these two are PM work that does not depend on CI, and leaving them open overnight would be a half-state.

### Q1 — the JSON-LD `BreadcrumbList` leaf: **A**, as implemented

Neither option touches a published contract, security, or gate strength, so this sits in the delegated code lane rather than the manual floor.

⭐ **First, the finding itself outranks the question.** `docsTrail()` builds `BreadcrumbList` from `source.pageTree`, and with `includePage: true` the leaf crumb *was* the page's tree node — the one node a `navTitle` replaces. So a short label would have reached the structured data a crawler reads, **on the exact surface epic #12243 exists to improve**, with no type, link, test or build failing. Nothing in `page.tsx` names `navTitle`, so the coupling is invisible from both ends. The card did not anticipate this consumer and neither did the dispatch order; finding it is the most valuable thing in this delivery.

On the fork itself, **A**:

- **Business need** — #12237 lengthens titles *for search intent*. A 55-character `headline` beside a 12-character breadcrumb leaf describes one page two ways to the same crawler, which is the opposite of what the epic is buying.
- **Long-term** — A removes a coupling instead of adding one: the JSON-LD stops depending on a page-tree transform it never mentions.
- **Hard to get wrong** — B's behaviour is discoverable only by reading rendered structured data. That is the failure mode this repo consistently designs against.
- **Scope** — one boolean.

⚠️ B's stated case — *"a breadcrumb IS a navigation surface"* — is the one part I weigh differently from the dev. It holds for a **rendered** breadcrumb; `docsTrail()` emits **JSON-LD for crawlers**, and the visible breadcrumb is a separate fumadocs-ui concern this option does not touch. So the reader-facing argument does not actually reach this call site, which makes A stronger than the report presents it.

The docblock correction matters and is right: *"a crumb and its sidebar entry are the same node with the same label"* is now true of **ancestors only**.

### Q2 — the key name: **`navTitle`**, and it stays free to change until #12237 lands

`sidebarTitle` is the more familiar spelling (Mintlify's), and that is a real argument for an authoring key. It loses on accuracy: the label replaces the **page-tree node name**, which feeds the sidebar, the prev/next footer navigation, *and* a folder that declares no `meta.json` title. A key named for one of three surfaces invites an author to reason about only that one — the same under-describing-name failure mode axis ③ exists to catch.

⚠️ Recorded for #12237 and the #12243 epic PM: **0 of 405 pages declare the key**, so this is a rename in 3 files plus 2 gates with **zero content migration** right up until the 176-row rewrite starts. After that it is 176 files. If the authors writing those rows prefer `sidebarTitle`, say so before that PR opens and it is nearly free.

### On the file-surface widening

Declared, and all three justified on inspection rather than accepted from the report: `check-doc-frontmatter.mjs` asserts set equality between `source.config.ts`'s extensions and its own key contracts and its self-test pinned *"the docs root is still handed `pageSchema` unextended"* — so extending the schema **forces** that edit; `lint.yml` is the new gate's step; `page.tsx` is Q1. Path surface read from `get_files`, ⛔ not the report: 8 files, **no governed surface** (`docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` all clear), so this lands through the merge queue rather than the governed four-step.

### Out-of-scope findings — both accepted as not-filed

The stale `403` in `check-doc-frontmatter.mjs`'s header (the corpus is 405, and the gate's own verdict line prints the live count) is correctly below the filing threshold: the number is incidental to the argument it supports, and a dated measurement two paragraphs above is legitimately dated. ⛔ Do not widen the prose diff in a busy gate file for it. The `apps/docs` no-test-infrastructure observation is right that it is idiom, not a gap — the app carries source-scanning gates of exactly this shape.

Card stays `pm:dispatched` until MERGED.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #14055. Verified against the tree and the checks, ⛔ not against the report

`domain:devx`, session `session_014iv4atze36k7F9C8oAe7QL`, R1. Reviewer of record.

### Checks — every one, ⛔ not the required subset

**29 check runs, all completed: 24 success, 5 skipped, 0 red, 0 pending** on head `a5eb6cc8d`. The five skips are path-filtered and legitimate for a diff that touches no package (`Build Core`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance`, `Console Pin Gate`, the dogfood matrix shard). `Governed Surface Queue Guard` = **success**, which independently confirms the path read below.

### Path fork — clean, so this lands through the queue

`get_files`, ⛔ not the report's self-description: 8 files, `+1070/−28`. No `docs/adr/**`, no `.claude/**`, no `skills/**`, no `AGENTS.md`, no `CLAUDE.md`. ⇒ ordinary ready → merge queue, not the governed four-step.

### Spot-checks — the four claims a green suite would not have caught

Each of these could have been false with everything still green, which is why they were read rather than accepted:

| claim | reading |
|---|---|
| the new gate is actually **invoked**, not just added | `lint.yml:1405-1406` — `--self-test` then the real run. A gate file that exists but is never called is the classic silent no-op |
| the resolver is the **single** resolution point with the fallback in it | `nav-title.ts:96-98` — `typeof … === 'string' ? .trim() : ''`, then `declared.length > 0 ? declared : data.title` |
| the plugin is **wired into `loader()`** | `source.ts:83` — `plugins: [lucideIconsPlugin(), navTitlePlugin()]`. Declared-but-inert was one of the four failure modes the card's own gate leg C exists for |
| **no consumer reads the key** | grep over the `apps/docs/app/**` and `lib/source.ts` diff: every `navTitle` occurrence is prose or the plugin import/registration. No `?? title` at a read site |

Changeset present and correctly scoped (`@objectstack/docs: patch`).

### ⭐ What makes this a better delivery than the card asked for

The card asked for a mechanism. What came back also carries **the reason the mechanism was dangerous**: the JSON-LD `BreadcrumbList` leaf was the page-tree node, so a short label would have reached crawler-visible structured data on the exact surface epic #12243 exists to improve — with no type, link, test or build failing, and nothing in `page.tsx` naming the key from either end. Adjudicated in the previous comment (option **A**), and now pinned by leg D so it cannot come back.

The dev also corrected the PM's own measurement in the card body: `generateMetadata` is four reads, not one, and `lib/source.ts:55` `getLLMText` is a seventh consumer the repaired body's table did not name — it is what `llms-full.txt` and the `/llms.mdx/docs/…` endpoints emit. ⇒ **Eleven read sites over six surfaces plus the page tree.** The dispatch asked for falsification of the PM's assumptions and got it; the card's table was understated and is now superseded by the PR body's.

### Deviations — all declared, all justified on inspection

The file surface widened by three files beyond the claim, each necessary rather than convenient: `check-doc-frontmatter.mjs` asserts set equality between `source.config.ts`'s extensions and its own key contracts and its self-test pinned *"the docs root is still handed `pageSchema` unextended"*, so extending the schema **forces** that edit; `lint.yml` is the new gate's step; `page.tsx` is the breadcrumb fix.
